item.text: {"question_id":"6B.8","answer":"During 2023, the Scholz coalition enacted or advanced several equal-rights measures, but practical enforcement and remedy remained uneven. Enacted measures included ending discriminatory blood-donation exclusions, ratifying the ILO Violence and Harassment Convention, adopting mandatory police-check records intended to address racial profiling, and increasing disability-employment fines from 2024; asylum seekers of all nationalities also became eligible for integration courses (BATCH-0001-E006; BATCH-0008-E011; BATCH-0008-E003; BATCH-0009-E019; BATCH-0011-R01-E006). These actions show federal commitment, but the supplied evidence does not establish their enforcement effects, actual course access or outcomes. The government also proposed legal gender-recognition reform, but this remained a bill under legislative review rather than an enacted 2023 protection, with unresolved concerns about children’s rights, parental consent, data protection and possible deterrence (BATCH-0001-E006; BATCH-0034-R04-E004; BATCH-0034-R04-E005). Practical equality was constrained by the coalition’s unadvanced promised expansion of the Anti-Discrimination Act, underfunded or insufficiently independent anti-discrimination bodies, inconsistent disability accessibility, employment and housing discrimination, and persistent gender-pay disparities (BATCH-0008-E002; BATCH-0009-E017; BATCH-0009-E019). Protection and remedy were also uneven for refugees and other vulnerable groups: eligible third-country nationals under temporary protection sometimes faced denial of registration, pressure into asylum procedures, and less favourable work and benefit access; no federal systematic vulnerability-screening procedure existed, protection practices varied by Land and municipality, and protection concepts were not generally binding or implementation-reviewed (BATCH-0011-R01-E008; BATCH-0011-R01-E009; BATCH-0011-R05-E002). Shelters lacked approximately 15,000 places, and LSBTIQ* reporting data indicated substantial underreporting linked partly to fear of police reactions, while recorded anti-LSBTIQ* crimes increased in 2023; these figures do not by themselves establish federal causation (BATCH-0009-E017; BATCH-0003-E006; BATCH-0003-E007). Distributional modelling suggested energy and social transfers supported lower-income households relatively more, but this was simulated rather than observed equality-outcome evidence (BATCH-0034-R12-E004). Overall, the period shows material legal and administrative steps toward equal dignity and opportunity, alongside significant gaps in accessibility, group-specific implementation, remedy and non-discrimination; national-level measures cannot be treated as proof of practical equality across affected
